To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have performed genome scale CRIPSR Cas9 screens in over 300 human cancer cell lines, developed a data driven prioritization framework to identify targets for cancer drug development and identified Werner syndrome as a synthetic lethal dependency in multiple cancer types with a high microsatellite instability phenotype.
we have developed a systematic target prioritisation framework to identify new drug targets for cancer and that we have validated one of these targets, WRN.

1) we performed genome-scale CRISPR Cas-9 screens in 323 cancer cell lines from multiple cancer types; 2) we developed a framework to prioritise new cancer drug targets based on their fitness effects, genomic biomarkers and tractability for drug discovery; 3) we identified the Werner syndrome helicase as a new cancer drug target for tumours with microsatellite instablility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new cancer targets and their validation in cancer cell lines and patient-derived xenografts.
the identification of new cancer therapeutic targets.
the identification of cancer dependencies and their application for drug target prioritization and validation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Werner syndrome ATP-dependent helicase is a synthetic lethal target that is a promising candidate for cancer therapeutics.
this study provides a resource of 324 cancer dependencies, generates an integrated data driven framework to prioritise cancer drug targets and suggest specific new targets.
we have identified the Werner syndrome ATP-dependent helicase as a synthetic lethal therapeutic target in tumours with microsatellite instabilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this study presents a resource of cancer cell line dependencies that can be used for target identification in cancer drug development, and a framework for target prioritization based on a combination of cell fitness effects, genomic biomarkers and tractability for drug discovery.

the integration of multiple data sets can be used to identify new cancer drug targets.
we developed a data driven approach that can prioritize new targets for cancer drug development, and that this approach can be applied to other disease areas.
